history.summary: Built in 1933 by Maharaja Kameshwar Singh of Darbhanga on the funeral pyre/cremation ghat of his father Maharaja Rameshwar Singh - a temple built on a pyre is itself unusual. The 10-foot black-stone idol of Maa Kali stands above the grave; the sanctum also holds Mahakal, Ganapati and Batukabhairava, and the goddess's mund-mala is said to carry the letters of the Hindi alphabet. The district site notes 6 temples around a central pond and counts it (with Kankali temple) among North Bihar's major tantric temples. The CSV name 'Shyama Kali Temple' is a documented alternate; the canonical name is Shyama Mai Temple (Kathalbari, LNMU campus, Darbhanga-846008).

name: Shyama Mai Temple
town_description: Darbhanga is a historic city in North Bihar, the old capital of the Mithila region and seat of the Darbhanga Raj. It is a cultural and educational centre, home to Lalit Narayan Mithila University.

travel.railway: Darbhanga Junction (temple is easily reached from the station, per the district site)
travel.road: At Kathalbari on the LNMU campus, Darbhanga; reachable by city road

visitor_information.best_time: October-November (Navaratri/Kali Puja) and December (annual Shyama Mai festival)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict: 4:00 AM-11:00 PM (meta.ai listing) vs 5:00 AM-10:00 PM (eindiatourism.in); no entry fee (verify before visiting)
